B: Hiya. Sorry, I thought the last one was my last one. I got myself muddled.
A: Ha, no worries. You hear me okay?
B: Yes, fine. I'm Joanne. Sutton-in-Ashfield.
A: Abdirahman. Leicester.
B: Oh, you're not far, then. We go to Leicester sometimes for the shops. What do you do?
A: Vehicle technician. Vans, at a fleet depot off the A6.
B: Oh, my partner Gary's a forklift driver. Warehouse off the M1. I bet you'd get on, he's always on about engines and that.
A: Yeah? What does he drive himself?
B: Erm, a Focus. Blue. I don't know what year. Sorry, that's not very helpful, is it.
A: Ha, that's alright. I've got an old Civic. Needs a clutch, actually. I'll probably do it myself, at the weekend.
B: You can do that at home?
A: If you've got the space and a bit of patience, yeah. Gearbox has to come down. Bit of a job, but it saves a few hundred quid, so.
B: Gosh. Gary changes the wipers and thinks he's done a service.
A: Ha. Most people are like that. What do you do?
B: I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. Serving dinners, washing up. I really like it, it fits round term time, and you get to know all the kids. They won't eat owt green, mind. Peas come back like they've not been touched. We just keep putting them out, you know, hoping one day.
A: My little sisters were like that. Still are, to be honest.
B: How old are they?
A: Seventeen and nineteen. I sort of keep an eye on them. My mum's ten minutes away.
B: Oh, that's nice. Mine's ten minutes away too. Her knees are playing up, so I go round and do her shopping.
A: Yeah, it's good having them close.
B: What do you have for your lunch at work, then? Sorry, I'm a dinner lady, I always ask about food.
A: Chicken cob, mostly. From the van outside. Or a meal deal.
B: A cob! Oh, thank goodness. Everybody's been saying barm and bap all afternoon. Cheese and onion cob, me.
A: Ha. Yeah, it's a cob. Don't know what else you'd call it.
B: That's what I said. Do you cook, at home?
A: Nah, Hodan does most of it. My wife. My job's the tea. Cardamom, loads of sugar.
B: Oh, that sounds lovely. Like a chai?
A: Sort of, yeah. Somali tea. My mum's is better than mine, but don't tell Hodan.
B: I won't. Do you watch the football? Gary's Mansfield.
A: Leicester City. Mansfield, though, fair play, they've done alright lately.
B: He'd be made up you said that. I go once a season to keep him company. I mostly look at the birds on the stand roof, if I'm honest.
A: Ha. Pigeons, yeah?
B: Gulls, sometimes. I sketch birds, you see. That's the robin in my...
